name: AVAIO Digital Taurus Hub (Brandon)
additional_info: 329-acre campus; Phase 1: 600,000 sqft, 116 MW from Entergy grid (energized June 2027). Path to 1+ GW: 420 MW additional grid power by end 2030, plus up to 500 MW onsite behind-the-meter gas generation (Gulf South Pipeline). Nearly 450 MW total expected online by 2027. 3rd largest investment in MS history. Broke ground Sept 10 2025. Yates Construction. Onsite generation tech: natural gas thermal (behind the meter, pipeline routing study complete).
source: AVAIO Digital press release, September 10, 2025: https://www.avaiodigital.com/updates/avaio-digital-breaks-ground-on-6-billion-brandon-data-center-campus-leading-mississippi-contractor-begins-site-work | Mississippi Development Authority, August 19, 2025: https://mississippi.org/news/avaio-digital-to-locate-6-billion-data-center-campus-in-rankin-county/
address: East Metropolitan Center Business and Industrial Park, Brandon, MS

name: AVAIO Digital Little Rock Campus
additional_info: 760-acre site in Little Rock, Pulaski County. Phase 1: 150 MW contracted with Entergy Arkansas. Full buildout: 1 GW potential, $21B total. Largest economic investment in Arkansas history. Announced Jan 12 2026. Water-efficient cooling, rainwater recapture, rooftop solar, cooling economization. 500+ permanent operations jobs over 5 years. Governor Huckabee Sanders statement.
source: AVAIO Digital press release, January 12, 2026: https://www.avaiodigital.com/news | Construction Dive, January 14, 2026: https://www.constructiondive.com/news/arkansas-data-center-campus-avaio-developer/809641/ | ENR, January 12, 2026: https://www.enr.com/articles/62325-26b-in-datacenter-builds-move-forward-in-arkansas-mississippi

name: Meta Hyperion Data Center Campus
additional_info: 4M sqft campus in Richland Parish (Holly Ridge area). 2 GW data center load; could scale to 5 GW as largest Meta facility. Broke ground December 2024; completion 2030. 9 buildings, 100% clean via Entergy Geaux Zero. Dedicated generation: 10 gas-fired plants totaling 7.5 GW (3 already approved + 7 new), 2,500 MW solar, 240 miles 500kV transmission. Meta funds all generation infrastructure. LPSC approved. $27B total investment per ENR Apr 2026. | Update March 2026: Meta announced 10 gas-fired power plants totaling 7.5 GW (3 previously approved + 7 new); total cost nearing $11B. Campus expanded to 2,250 acres plus 1,400 additional acres acquired early 2026. LPSC approval still required for new generation.
source: Data Center Dynamics, March 31, 2026: https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/meta-announces-4-million-sq-ft-louisiana-data-center-campus/ | NOLA.com, March 27, 2026: https://www.nola.com/news/business/entergy-power-meta-ai-data-center/article_4509eaa2-45a1-4d28-9482-fa1c6bed80de.html | ENR, April 2, 2026: https://www.enr.com/articles/62766-27b-meta-data-center-pushes-louisiana-toward-massive-power-expansion | STRisker Daily Notes, March 30, 2026: https://writing.strisker.com/data-centers-daily-notes-march-30-2026/

name: Meta Hyperion Data Center Campus Expansion
additional_info: Meta is expanding its Hyperion AI supercluster data center in Richland Parish, Louisiana, from 2 GW to 5 GW of compute capacity, with total investment surpassing $50 billion.
address: Richland Parish, LA
transmission_upgrades.description: Construction of 10 new gas-fired power plants by Entergy Louisiana to meet energy demands.

name: Amazon Web Services Louisiana Campus
additional_info: $12B Amazon Louisiana data center network. Construction to begin 2026. Specific parish/county not publicly confirmed as of May 2026.

name: Cloverleaf Infrastructure Troy Data Center Campus
additional_info: 250-300 acres near St. Louis (Troy area). Up to 500 MW at full buildout. Multiple data center buildings. Part of Missouri secondary market emergence driven by central US location and fiber connectivity.

name: Armory Innovation District Data Center (St. Louis)
developer: Contour / TeraWatt / THO Investments / Steadfast City
additional_info: 120 MW data center at Macy's/Famous-Barr warehouse adjacent to historic Armory building (1 N. Jefferson, St. Louis). Part of $3B Armory Innovation District redevelopment — Armory building converted to office space. Conditional use permit approved by St. Louis Board of Public Service April 21, 2026 (final OK), despite Mayor Spencer's request for delay three weeks prior. Strong community opposition at public comment. Qualifies for Ameren Missouri new hyperscale rate structure (above 75 MW). Developers: Contour, TeraWatt, THO Investments, Steadfast City, ARCO, Lewis Rice.

name: Applied Digital Deuel County (Toronto)
additional_info: $5B, 430 MW, two buildings ~907,500 sqft each. East of Toronto, near Otter Tail Power transmission lines and Astoria gas plant. Paused after SD Legislature rejected sales tax exemption Mar 2026. No land purchased, no zoning filed. Monitoring elections. 200 permanent jobs projected. Total investment impact potentially $10-16B.
address: East of Toronto, Deuel County, SD 57268

name: Hut 8 Latham
additional_info: Large scale compute/AI infrastructure.

name: CyrusOne Springfield (Sangamon County)
additional_info: 600 MW campus in Springfield. Sangamon County Board approved $500M data center project. CyrusOne seeking approval. Grandfathered under Illinois tax incentive program (pre-July 2026 suspension).
address: Springfield, Sangamon County, IL

name: Pekin Data Center (withdrawn)
additional_info: City had already signed real estate purchase contract with Pekin I Developer LLC for $4.5M. Mayor Mary Burress announced March 9, 2026 that city would not move forward. Announcement drew thunderous applause at public meeting. Contract termination details pending.
address: North of Lutticken Lake, Pekin, Tazewell County, IL

name: Vantage Lighthouse Campus (Stargate Wisconsin)
additional_info: 672 acres. Four single-story buildings, 2.5M sqft, 902 MW. Largest private investment in Wisconsin history. Groundbreaking December 17, 2025. Tenants: Oracle + OpenAI (Stargate). $8B Phase 1 contractors: Whiting-Turner, Weitz, Michels, Turner-McCarthy JV. 4,000+ union construction jobs. 70% zero-emission energy via We Energies. $3M Lakeshore Natural Resource Partnership for Valley Creek restoration.
address: North side of Port Washington, Ozaukee County, WI (adjacent to I-43, ~27 miles north of Milwaukee; 672 acres)
transmission_upgrades.description: American Transmission Company Ozaukee Distribution Interconnection Project; community attempting to recall mayor for supporting project

name: Dewberry Engineers / Undisclosed Developer Caledonia Data Center
additional_info: 244.7-acre site on northern edge of Racine County. Virginia-based Dewberry Engineers filed rezoning and land use amendment for the site. ~6 miles south of Microsoft Mount Pleasant campus. Reported July 31, 2025.
address: South of Douglas Avenue and County Line Road, west of Oak Creek Power Plant, Caledonia, Racine County, WI

name: Kenosha Data Center (undisclosed)
additional_info: Kenosha Plan Commission unanimously approved plans to annex and rezone land November 21, 2024. Pending city council approval. Land to be rezoned to manufacturing. Located ~6 miles south of Microsoft Mount Pleasant (Foxconn site) data center. Developer identity not disclosed.
address: Northwest of I-94 and State Highway 142, Kenosha, WI (annexed from Town of Paris)

name: Oracle / OpenAI / Related Digital Saline Township Data Center (Stargate Michigan)
additional_info: 1.4 GW, 250 acres, 2.2M sqft. Largest one-time investment in Michigan history per Gov. Whitmer. Michigan PSC approved DTE Electric long-term power contracts with Oracle subsidiary Green Chile Ventures LLC. Saline Township dropped objections as part of legal settlement. Construction to begin Q1 2026 pending environmental permits. 2,500 union construction jobs; 450 permanent jobs. Part of Stargate initiative.
source: Crain's Detroit Business, January 2, 2026: https://www.crainsdetroit.com/technology/these-data-center-projects-are-pending-across-michigan | Michigan Public Radio, October 30, 2025: https://www.michiganpublic.org/economy/2025-10-30/massive-data-center-project-announced-for-michigan
address: Saline Township, Washtenaw County, MI (near Ann Arbor)
transmission_upgrades.description: DTE Electric long-term power contracts approved by Michigan PSC after Saline Township dropped objections via legal settlement

name: Meta Elmore Township Data Center (On Hold — moratorium)
additional_info: 1,077-acre multi-phase campus. $1B+ investment per phase. Rezoning request withdrawn December 2025 after township board passed 6-month pause on data centers (MLive reported). Power usage unknown. Developer described as supported by Meta. Township expected to revisit after moratorium expires mid-2026.
address: Elmore Township, MI (1,077-acre site)

name: Microsoft Gaines Township Data Center (On Hold)
additional_info: Request to rezone 356-acre site in Kent County's Gaines Township. Microsoft has not yet submitted a site plan — township approval required at future meeting. Facility size and power usage unknown. On hold as of early 2026.
address: Gaines Township, Kent County, MI

name: University of Michigan / Los Alamos AI Research Campus (Ypsilanti Township)
developer: University of Michigan / Los Alamos National Laboratory
additional_info: $1.25B AI research and high-performance computing campus. Joint venture between University of Michigan and Los Alamos National Laboratory. Rezoning request pending with Ypsilanti Township planning commission.
address: Ypsilanti Township, Washtenaw County, MI

name: Thor Equities Augusta Township Data Center
additional_info: 810-acre site in Augusta Township. Township board approved rezoning request, but residents organizing a referendum to overturn the approval. On hold pending referendum outcome.
address: Augusta Township, Washtenaw County, MI (810 acres)

name: Franklin Partners Lowell Township Data Center (On Hold)
additional_info: Franklin Partners requested pause on its data center rezoning application. Company said it was in talks with an American-owned company interested in locating a data center there. On hold as of early 2026 pending continued negotiations.
address: Lowell Township, Kent County, MI

name: Sentinel Project Shirley Eagle Creek (Lake County)
additional_info: $5B investment by Sentinel (Project Shirley). Multiple data center buildings planned. NIPSCO expects 8.6 GW of data center demand across their system by 2035. Community opposition involves rising NIPSCO electricity bills ($77/month increase per 1,000 kWh over past 2 years). IURC received more complaints about NIPSCO in 2026 YTD than all of 2025.
address: Eagle Creek Township, Lake County, IN

name: Amazon Hobart Data Center (Lake County)
additional_info: $11B Amazon data center in Hobart (northwest border community near Chicago). Mayor and City Council unanimously approved. Third data center in northwest Indiana NIPSCO service area. Contentious regional context: rising NIPSCO bills, concerns about data center cost-shifting.
address: Hobart, Lake County, IN

name: Amazon Web Services Northwest Indiana Expansion (Phase 2)
additional_info: $15B additional investment announced November 24, 2025. 2.4 GW additional capacity. New campuses across Northwest Indiana separate from New Carlisle Phase 1. Partners: State of Indiana, IEDC, NIPSCO. Exact locations not yet disclosed — Amazon indicated sites to be selected soon. Brings combined IN commitment to $26B+.
address: Northwest Indiana (exact counties/municipalities TBD as of May 2026; NIPSCO service territory)

name: Microsoft La Porte Data Center
additional_info: $1B data center announced June 2024. Gov. Holcomb announcement. Microsoft is fourth major tech company to announce IN investment in 2024 (alongside Meta $800M Jeffersonville, Google $2B Fort Wayne, Amazon $11B New Carlisle). Entitlement phase / pre-construction. Construction expected late 2025-2026. (Note: DCD refers to Mishawaka, Blackridge to La Porte — La Porte is primary confirmed.)
source: Indiana Public Media / IPM, June 4, 2024: https://www.ipm.org/2024-06-04/microsoft-plans-1-billion-data-center-in-northwest-indiana | Blackridge Research IN: https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/latest-list-top-new-data-centers-in-indiana-united-states-us
address: La Porte, La Porte County, IN

name: Google Indianapolis Data Center (rejected)
additional_info: Major Google data center proposal for Indianapolis rejected by Indianapolis City/County planning officials. One of at least three data center rejections by local officials in Indiana within four months (alongside St. Joseph County New Carlisle and Prologis Shelbyville).
address: Indianapolis, Marion County, IN

name: Prologis Shelbyville Data Center (unfavorable recommendation)
additional_info: ~500-acre annexation approved by Shelbyville City Council earlier. Planning commission issued "unfavorable" recommendation after 5-hour hearing with overwhelming resident opposition. Third data center rejection by local officials in Indiana in four months. Final approval pending city council vote.
address: Shelbyville, Shelby County, IN

name: Meta Jeffersonville Data Center
additional_info: $800M, 700,000 sqft. Construction underway by Turner Construction. Expected completion 2026. Meta's earliest Indiana project. Located in Clark County just north of Louisville, KY.
source: Data Center Frontier, May 2024: https://datacenterfrontier.com/site-selection/article/55036862/with-almost-14-billion-in-announced-spending-data-centers-call-indiana-home | Blackridge Research IN: https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/latest-list-top-new-data-centers-in-indiana-united-states-us
address: Jeffersonville, Clark County, IN

name: RadiusDC Plainfield Data Centers
additional_info: Two data centers planned in Plainfield, Hendricks County (suburban Indianapolis, southwest). MW and investment not disclosed. Part of broader Indiana data center buildout per Construction Review Online January 2026.
address: Plainfield, Hendricks County, IN

name: TeraWulf Justified Data Campus
phase: Initial 401 MW Anthropic AI/HPC lease within 482 MW electric-service capacity
transmission_utility: Big Rivers Electric Corporation / Kenergy Corp.
ownership_transfers: TeraWulf acquired and is redeveloping the former Century Aluminum smelter site.
additional_info: AI/HPC data center campus in Hawesville with a 20-year Anthropic lease for approximately 401 MW of critical IT load. Kentucky PSC-approved service supports up to 482 MW.
address: Former Century Aluminum smelter site, Hawesville, Hancock County, KY

name: Google Project Pyramid (West Memphis)
additional_info: Google's West Memphis campus is under construction. A September 1 disclosure reported that service is expected to begin in February 2027 and ramp to a maximum contracted demand of 600 MW by October 2029; Google will fund $526 million toward Cypress Solar and $190 million of transmission upgrades. 1,178-acre site; 5 data center buildings + office space + on-site substation across ~580 acres. Largest private investment in Arkansas history. Groundbreaking ceremony October 2025 with Gov. Sanders. Google to invest $4B through 2027. 300 permanent jobs, 5,000+ construction jobs. Property tax revenue ~$120M for local schools. APSC approved 600 MW solar + 350 MW battery storage (Entergy Arkansas) October 2025. Google $25M Energy Impact Fund for Crittenden County affordability. Demand-response "load flexibility" contract with Entergy. Google confirmed September 2025 after operating under Groot LLC / Project Pyramid codename.
source: Axios (2026-09-01) | Data Center Dynamics, September 9, 2025: https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/google-confirmed-to-be-behind-west-memphis-data-center-project-in-arkansas/ | State Gazette (West Memphis), October 9, 2025: https://www.stategazette.com/news/delta-goes-digital-as-google-plants-roots-in-west-memphis/article_9dd19d21-970a-56c4-8895-4b9278155e32.html | Arkansas PSC approval, October 3, 2025: https://pv-magazine-usa.com/2025/10/03/arkansas-to-build-600-mw-solar-project-for-googles-4b-data-center/
address: West Memphis, Crittenden County, AR
transmission_upgrades.description: Google is reported to pay $190 million for transmission upgrades associated with service to the West Memphis campus.
